newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia rural exports to rise 1.2 pct-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia rural exports to rise 1.2 pct-ABARE.

text.p: The value of Australian rural exports is forecast to rise by 1.2 percent in 1997/98 to A$22.8 billion from A$22.5 billion in 1996/97 (July-June), the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said at its Outlook conference on Tuesday.

ABARE said total rural exports include forest and fisheries products, which are expected to show a slight rise next financial year. But the bulk of Australian rural exports, which are derived from the farm sector, show a flat to decliing trend.
The value of farm exports in 1997/98 is forecast to be A$20.19 billion, steady with the previous year which was down 1.1 percent on the 1995/96 level.

The flat outlook for the next financial year is primarily due to the 21 percent fall in the expected value of wheat exports with lower exported volumes and prices, ABARE's executive director Brian Fisher said in presenting a commodities overview outlook at the conference.
ABARE is Australia's official commodity forecaster.
"No growth is expected in (Australian) farm export earnings in 1997/98," Fisher said.
ABARE had held its forecast of Australia's 1996/97 farm exports virtually steady with its forecast last December at A$20.2 billion, down 1.1 percent on the previous year.
The value of Australian wheat exports is forecast to fall by 10.0 percent to A$3.0 billion in 1996/97, in line with ABARE's December forecast.
But the 1997/98 value of wheat exports is forecast to fall 21.0 percent after a decline in export volume to 13.0 million tonnes from 15.5 million tonnes in 1996/97, Fisher said.

A turnaround in the export performance of the wool and beef industries in 1997/98, after declines in the value of exports in 1996/97, is not expected to be enough to offset the forecast fall in the value of wheat exports, he said.
Export earnings of dairy products and cotton are forecast to rise strongly in both 1996/97 and 1997/98, largely as a result of increased volumes, he said.
The value of sugar exports is forecast to be down, reflecting lower world prices in 1996/97 and 1997/98, he said.

The forecast export price for the benchmark wheat grade Australian Standard White was forecast to fall to A$176.00 a tonne in nominal terms in 1997/98 from A$188.00 a tonne in 1996/97 and from A$259.00 in 1995/96.

The nominal value of wool exports in 1997/98 is forecast to rise to A$3.77 billion from A$3.48 billion the year before. This was after a slip in volume exported to 834,000 tonnes from 849,000 tonnes, but a recovery in nominal auction prices to 650 cents a kg in 1997/98 from 600 cents a kg in 1996/97.
The value of Australian meat exports in 1997/98 is forecast to rise to A$2.40 billion from A$2.06 billion after a price recovery.
Australian dairy exports in 1997/98 are forecast to rise to A$2.15 billion in 1997/98 from A$1.94 billion this year.
Cotton exports are forecast to rise to A$1.11 billion in 1997/98 from A$903.0 million the year before on increased export volume and prices.
The value of Australian sugar exports in 1997/98 is forecast to fall to A$1.36 billion from A$1.42 billion in nominal terms after increased production but falling prices.
